title: SEED: a measurement protocol for agentic software work, with the PR case study 'Throughput is not progress'
description: Implementation throughput is a poor proxy for verified progress in agent-driven software work. SEED records that finding as a small, incident-bounded protocol: claims have falsifiers, guards are sabotage-tested before they are trusted, state lives in git artifacts, humans gate only irreversibles, and spend is scored against closed loops. The bundled PR case study (1,979 PR-linked commits on one pinned repository) is author-run and not independently reproduced; whether using SEED improves recovery time, false-progress rate, or human intervention versus a bare project is a registered hypothesis (C-004) and is not claimed.
notes: Version 0.1.0 is the first public identity of this repository (formerly Bonkers). The case study is n=1 repository, n=1 principal, author-run.
